subject: Acme: Clarify how DSRs affect invoice & usage record availability
messages:
From: Dana Liu <procurement@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: If a user requests deletion, will Acme still be able to access prior invoices and per-user usage records?

Hi Jonas,

Quick one from our legal/procurement review: Acme has a handful of users who might submit Data Subject Requests for erasure. We need to confirm whether those DSRs would remove any billing artifacts that we rely on for reconciliation and chargebacks (line-item usage, per-user token logs tied to invoices).

Specifically:
- Will invoices and invoice PDFs still be available to Acme after we process a customer deletion?
- Are there any circumstances where token-level usage entries that feed invoices are removed or redacted?
- If certain usage rows are removed for privacy reasons, what is Redwood's recommended reconciliation workflow so we don't lose auditability for month-end?

We appreciate a short, concrete response we can pass to our finance team.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Procurement Manager, Acme IoT
procurement@acme.com

---
Note: please copy our billing lead Peter Shaw on replies (peter.shaw@acme.com).

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: If a user requests deletion, will Acme still be able to access prior invoices and per-user usage records?

Dana —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:
- Invoices and invoice PDFs (the finalized monthly statements) are preserved for accounting and tax compliance and remain available to the customer even after a DSR.
- Token-level raw logs that contain personal data may be subject to erasure in limited cases; however, we retain a separate billing ledger used for invoicing that is preserved to meet accounting obligations.

I'll let Marissa and Neha add the formal finance/legal phrasing and any exceptions. Below I've outlined the operational expectations so Acme can plan reconciliation.

Operational notes:
1) Invoice preservation: We snapshot and store finalized invoice artifacts (PDFs, invoice numbers, totals, tax lines) in a billing ledger that is not deleted on individual DSRs. Those artifacts are used for tax and audit and are available in the console and via invoice exports.

2) Usage records vs. billing ledger: We maintain two related datasets: the raw usage events (per-token, per-request logs) and a derived billing ledger (aggregated line items and billed units). When a DSR requires erasure of personal data in raw usage logs, we do not retroactively delete entries from the billing ledger; instead we mark the raw log rows as redacted where required and keep the ledger intact for accounting.

3) Reconciliation guidance: If Acme relies on per-user mappings, we recommend exporting the monthly invoice (PDF + CSV line items) and retaining a local mapping between your internal user IDs and invoice line items. If a user is erased and your mapping is lost, the invoice still shows the billed units but you may lose the direct per-user attribution unless you capture it before deletion.

Marissa — can you confirm exceptions (legal hold, tax jurisdiction differences, or specific compliance requests) and attach the short retention summary?

Cheers,
Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <procurement@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: If a user requests deletion, will Acme still be able to access prior invoices and per-user usage records?

Dana / team —

Adding the finance/legal position and attaching the short PDF that summarizes invoice retention and the DSR interplay (attached: Redwood_Invoice_Retention_Summary.pdf). Key points:

- Finalized invoices: Retained for a minimum of 7 years (or longer where local tax law requires) and are not deleted in response to individual DSRs, because they are necessary for tax records and accounting. This includes the PDF and the ledger entries that compose the invoice.

- Raw usage logs: May contain personally identifiable data and are treated under our Data Retention & Erasure policy. Where erasure is required we will redact personal identifiers in those logs. However, aggregated or pseudonymized billing ledgers used to compute invoices are preserved.

- Legal hold & audits: If Acme requests a legal hold tied to an audit or dispute, submit that request to support@redwood.ai; we will suspend deletion and preserve relevant artifacts while the hold is active.

- Reconciliation: We recommend the following workflow so you retain per-user chargeback capability even after DSRs:
  1) Export monthly invoice CSVs and a per-batch usage export at month close.
  2) Store a short-lived mapping of internal user IDs to exported usage rows in your systems for the period needed for internal chargeback.
  3) If a DSR is received, proceed with erasure of personal identifiers in raw logs as required, but use the preserved invoice CSVs for accounting.

Attachment: ACME_Invoice_20270331.pdf (sample invoice)

If you want, we can run a short session with your finance team next week to walk through exports and the console locations for invoice/ledger downloads.

Best,
Marissa Cole
